full_judgment:
4. The petitioner contested the Arbitration case by filing written objection traversing all the material allegation made in the arbitration case. It was stated that the award of compensation by the Deputy Commissioner was prepared keeping in consideration the provisions contained in section 8 of the said Ordinance and the respondent No. 3 accepted the compensation money without any objection or protest and respondent No. 3 was debarred from filing any application under section 28 of the Ordinance before the Arbitrator. It was further stated that the Arbitration case was barred by limitation. 

 5. Learned Arbitrator by the judgment and order dated 14-3-91 gave an award enhancing Taka 87,82,573, 06 from Taka 19,69,056.85 as compensation for the acquired land and directed the requiring body and the Deputy Commissioner to pay Taka 68,13,516.08 within 60 days. The petitioner felt aggrieved by the said award and sought setting aside the same through a medium of appeal before the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal. As there was a delay of 18 days in preferring appeal an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act had been filed for condonation of delay. 

 6. The Arbitration Appellate Tribunal by the order dated 31-1-93 rejected the prayer for condonation of delay and at the same time dismissed the appeal as being barred by limitation. 

 11. Mr KM Saifuddin Ahmed, learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing in support of the Rule, contended that the learned Arbitration Appellate Tribunal committed gross illegality in not condoning the delay and dismissing the appeal as being barred by limitation. It was the further contention of learned Deputy Attorney-General that the respondent No. 3 having received the compensation money without any objection he was debarred from filing an application before the learned Arbitrator and the Arbitration case was not maintainable. 

 12. Mr. Ozair Farooq, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent Nos. 3(a)- 3(h) contended that since the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 is a special law the general law of limitation i.e., section 5 of the Limitation Act, will not apply in the matter of condonation of delay. In support of his contention reliance has been placed upon a decision in the case of Ishaque (Md) and others vs. Government of Bangladesh reported in 43 DLR (AD) 28. 

 14. From a plain reading of section 34 of the Ordinance it is manifestly clear that no special period of limitation for preferring an appeal before the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal has been prescribed. The Ordinance No. II of 1982 is a special law. As such in the absence of any such special period of limitation prescribed in the Ordinance for preferring an appeal before the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal, general law of limitation codified in the Limitation Act comes into play and section 5 of the Limitation Act is applicable in such cases. 

 15. Mr. Ozair Farooq, the learned Advocate though argued that by way of amendment in section 34 of the Ordinance special period of limitation had been prescribed but failed to show that a special period of limitation has been prescribed by way of any subsequent amendment in section 34 of the Ordinance. We are not aware of any such amendment made in section 34 of the Ordinance prescribing a special period of limitation. Though some amendments had been made in various sections of the said Ordinance the latest amendment being on 1-12-94 by the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property (Amendment) Act, 1994. 

 16. In the case of Ishaque (Md) and others vs. Government of Bangladesh 43 DLR (AD) 28 relied upon by Mr. Ozair Farooq learned Advocate for respondent No. 3 in support of his contention as to the non applicability of section 5 of Limitation Act in an appeal under section 34 of the Ordinance the lands in question were acquired by the Government under the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 and Ishaque and others whose land were acquired being dissatisfied with the compensation assessed filed Arbitration cases before the Fourth Court of Subordinate Judge and Arbitrator, Dhaka. Final awards were passed and against those awards the Government preferred two Miscellaneous Appeals below the Hip court Division under section 7(f) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 read with Rule 9(16) (Emergency) Requisition of Property Rules, 1948 which prescribed a period of 60 days for filing such appeal. Those two appeals were barred by 48 days. The learned Judges of the High Court Division condoned the delay under section 5 of the Limitation Act. Leave were granted in two civil petitions for leave to appeal and those were numbered as Civil Appeal Nos. 13 and 14 of 1990. On the question that has been raised in those cases relating to the applicability of section 5 of the Limitation Act in view of sub-section 2 of section 29 of the Limitation Act their Lordships of the Appellate Division held that section 5 of the Limitation Act is excluded in determining the period of limitation for an appeal under the special law. In the said cases appeals were filed under sub-rule 16 of Rule 9 of (Emergency) Requisition of Property Rules, 1948 which prescribed a period of 60 days in filing an appeal. In the said Rules of 1948 a special period of limitation was prescribed in filing an appeal and in view of the specific provision of law their Lordships of the Appellate Division held that section 5 of the Limitation Act got no application to special law. But in this instant case before us there is nothing to show that a special period of limitation in filing an appeal either in the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 or in the Acquisition of Immovable Property Rules, 1982 framed under the Ordinance has been prescribed. Thus the facts and circumstances of those cases are quite distinguishable and got no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of this instant case. So Mr. Ozair Farooq cannot have any assistance of the cited decision. 

 17. On going through the Arbitration case record which had been called for by this court it appears that there had been a delay of only 18 days and that delay was explained in the application filed under section 5 of the Limitation Act. The explanation was that in view of the pendency of hundreds of arbitration cases and arbitration appeals the concerned file of the case was misplaced and, as such, there was a delay of days in filing the appeal. 

 18. It appears from the record that the petitioner on 31-1-1993 filed an application for an adjournment of the hearing of the condonation matter. The Arbitration Appellate Tribunal in disposing of the said application not only rejected the same but also disposed of the application for condonation of delay on merit and at the same time dismissed the appeal as being barred by limitation without assigning any satisfactory or cogent reason. The Arbitration Appellate Tribunal did not feel it fit to consider the petitioner''s prayer with application of judicial mind required by a court dispensing justice and equity. In the facts and circumstances of this case and in the interest of justice it will not be fair to deprive the Government petitioner of the right of appeal. Our considered view is that the grounds taken by the petitioner in the application for condonation of delay are satisfactory, reasonable and acceptable and the decision of the Appellate Tribunal suffers from clear impropriety.
